summary:
The next giant leap on the Moon begins long before touchdown. It begins with choosing where to land.

Team Altius developed SelenEkto, an interactive lunar exploration application that transforms complex scientific data into meaningful insights for evaluating potential landing sites on the Moon's south pole.

Using real NASA datasets, we built a Python-based desktop application that allows users to explore lunar terrain, visualise elevation and slope, analyse terrain horizons and compare landing locations. By integrating NASA/JPL Horizons, we also enabled users to investigate solar positions and estimate sunlight availability across different locations and time periods.

Our development combined scientific research, computational problem-solving and software engineering. We processed large datasets, built analytical tools, created interactive visualisations and overcame challenges involving coordinate systems, data accuracy and application performance. We ultimately packaged SelenEkto into a portable Windows application with an offline data library.

SelenEkto brings multiple landing-site considerations into one accessible platform, making complex lunar data easier to explore, understand and compare.
details:
The next giant leap on the Moon begins long before touchdown. It begins with choosing where to land.

SelenEkto, developed by Team Altius, is an interactive lunar exploration and landing-site analysis application that makes complex NASA scientific data accessible, visual and easier to interpret.

Our project brings together lunar topography, terrain measurements, solar positions and candidate-site comparisons in a single Python-based desktop application. Instead of navigating separate scientific datasets, users can explore the Moon's south pole, inspect terrain conditions and investigate factors that could influence future landing-site selection.

How SelenEkto Works

SelenEkto processes high-resolution lunar terrain data obtained from NASA's Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) resources. Our application provides several integrated features:

  • Terrain Explorer: Visualises lunar surface elevation, slope and observation coverage, allowing users to examine specific areas and save potential landing locations.
  • Solar and Horizon Analysis: Uses NASA/JPL Horizons ephemeris data alongside local terrain-horizon calculations to investigate potential sunlight obstruction over selected time periods.
  • Landing-Site Comparison: Allows users to compare candidate locations using terrain measurements, visualisations and adjustable comparison priorities.
  • Data Library: Provides 24 offline lunar slope previews, with additional high-resolution NASA datasets available for selective download.
  • Data Transparency: Identifies missing or incomplete datasets, helping users distinguish reliable measurements from unavailable or preliminary information.

Our Development Process

Our development combined scientific research, mathematical reasoning, programming and extensive problem-solving.

We investigated the scientific challenges surrounding lunar landing-site selection, researched NASA's available data resources and translated our findings into technical requirements.

Using Python, we developed data-processing scripts, terrain-analysis functions and a graphical application built with PySide6. Libraries including NumPy, Rasterio, PyProj and Matplotlib enabled us to process geographical data, perform calculations and produce interactive visualisations.

We used Visual Studio Code for development, Git and GitHub for version control, and PyInstaller to package the application into a portable Windows executable.

Throughout development, we addressed problems involving large dataset handling, coordinate transformations, missing data, software reliability and scientific uncertainty.

Innovation and Intended Impact

What distinguishes SelenEkto is its integration of multiple scientific considerations into one accessible environment.

Rather than presenting a static map or automatically declaring a location safe, our application allows users to investigate the underlying evidence and compare locations according to different priorities.

Our team considered terrain steepness, elevation, observation coverage, solar visibility, data quality, computational performance and accessibility. We also recognised that preliminary scientific estimates require further validation before operational use.

SelenEkto is intended as a research and educational tool, helping students, researchers and space enthusiasts understand the complexities of lunar exploration.

Ultimately, Team Altius aims to bridge the gap between advanced planetary science and accessible technology, demonstrating how thoughtful software engineering can transform scientific datasets into meaningful, interactive insights.
